collection_method: Read-only GitHub issue search and issue/comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded snippets were treated as evidence and not executed. No attachments, linked demonstrations or code files, packages, agent runtimes, reproduction steps, target systems, or external tools were opened or run.

selected_records.title: HandoffMessage.context splices peer-authored messages into another agent's model context with their declared LLM role intact
selected_records.provider_attribution: Microsoft AutoGen framework surface; the model-compliance hop was a deterministic stub, so no model provider is attributed.
selected_records.assessment: A public adversarial reproduction demonstrates that a custom participant can hand off peer-authored context with a privileged role and choose the receiving agent. The receiving framework path and tool execution were reported as unmodified, but the victim model's compliance was deliberately stubbed. This is a strong transfer/use and boundary-control demonstration, not an observed autonomous incident or a new rogue swarm.

selected_records.title: [BUG] A2A - completed requested ignored
selected_records.provider_attribution: CrewAI A2A integration and a reporter-described remote implementation; no model provider attribution.
selected_records.assessment: A reporter describes a remote agent returning the same completed result while the local server repeatedly delegates the same request until its turn limit. A contributor characterized the local status handling as designed and added a flag. This is an intentional A2A exchange with a completion-handling defect, not rogue coordination.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: autogen.agentchat.register_function adds to all Agents instead of single
selected_records.provider_attribution: Microsoft AutoGen configuration behavior; no model provider attribution.
selected_records.assessment: The reproduction reports a function definition appearing in another configured agent because both agents shared the same mutable configuration object. It is a configuration-isolation control, not an inter-agent exchange.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: Agents inventing their own names, calling each other wrong names. Changing their names in between 2 answers
selected_records.provider_attribution: Reporter-configured AutoGen group chat; no independent participant or provider verification.
selected_records.assessment: Name and role drift in a designed group chat does not authenticate distinct actors or show a transferred task result. It is an identity-label reliability control.

selected_records.title: Graphflow bug finding next speaker when an agent has tools
selected_records.provider_attribution: Microsoft AutoGen GraphFlow with a reporter-declared OpenAI model; execution provenance is not independently verified.
selected_records.assessment: A configured multi-agent graph reportedly failed to select the next speaker after a tool-bearing agent ran. This is a routing failure inside an intentionally defined workflow, with no preserved result-use chain or unauthorized coordination.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. Every selected record was already public before collection; the strongest boundary chain is a synthetic adversarial demonstration, and the only concrete remote-agent exchange is an intentional A2A workflow.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap heavily; this is not a repository census.
GitHub issue text and comments are reporter assertions, not authenticated agent telemetry.
Open issue state and recent comments do not establish ongoing autonomous activity.
No attachments, external reproductions, packages, linked code files, agent runtimes, or linked target systems were opened or executed; embedded issue snippets were not run.
Issue bodies may change after the recorded observation; hashes cover the body text returned at collection time.

Advancement requires an original, not-previously-published exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, actual task-result transfer and recipient use, plus evidence that the coordination exceeded operator authorization in a real run rather than a designed workflow or synthetic test.
redactions: No payload bodies, credentials, personal addresses, sink identifiers, tokens, or private logs are included.
Assessments summarize incident shape without reproducing executable demonstrations or tool-call content.
